title: TabPFN: a pretrained tabular model against tuned boosting
request: Find out whether a pretrained tabular foundation model (TabPFN v2 and v3) matches or beats tuned gradient boosting with no tuning, and at what cost in latency and data size.
spec: A training script and a benchmark of TabPFN (v2, v3, and v3 in thinking mode) against trees, scikit-learn models and lucidrains TabTransformer/FT-Transformer on Telco churn and HyperAck.
plan: Write train_tabpfn.py (v2 without a token, v3 with one) and benchmark_tabpfn.py.
Run both datasets and record ROC-AUC per model.
Compare with the churn campaign and the HyperAck safe champion.

decisions.decision: Keep the TabPFN token in the repository-root .env, never in code or chat.
decisions.why: v3 and thinking mode call a hosted service that needs the token.

change: research/tabular-foundation-models/experiments/tabpfn/ with the training script, the benchmark, a notebook and results (benchmark.csv, metrics.json, thinking_metrics.json).

findings.defect: The HyperAck loader of the TabPFN benchmark keeps the two post-outcome final fares.
findings.scenario: load_part1 in train_tabpfn.py passes final_customer_fare and final_biker_fare to every model, so TabPFN's HyperAck ROC-AUC of 0.981 (histogram boosting 0.973) is leakage-inflated; the honest safe champion on that data is 0.9455.
findings.cause: The loader was written before the safe-vs-unsafe analysis and never got the HyperAck contract.
findings.fix: Found during the repository reorganization (2026-10-03); the track README now carries a warning that the HyperAck rows are inflated, and a rerun without the fares is queued as the track's next step (it needs TabPFN, torch and the token).
findings.impact: Read at face value, the benchmark says TabPFN reaches 0.981 on HyperAck, far above the honest champion of 0.9455; anyone choosing a foundation model from it would be choosing on a leak.
findings.open: The rerun has not happened (it needs TabPFN, torch and the token), so the track has no leakage-safe HyperAck result for TabPFN.

measurements.name: TabPFN benchmark on Telco churn
measurements.gate: Same split for every model; compare ROC-AUC.
measurements.result: TabPFN in thinking mode 0.850 on the full training set (fit 254.2 s); logistic regression 0.841 and XGBoost 0.841 on the full training set (fit 0.069 s for logistic regression); TabPFN-2 0.841 with only 1,024 training rows as context.
measurements.next: Repeat on leakage-safe HyperAck before drawing any conclusion about foundation models.
measurements.against_gate: There is no threshold: TabPFN in thinking mode leads at 0.850, logistic regression and XGBoost reach 0.841 on the full training set, and TabPFN-2 reaches 0.841 from only 1,024 context rows. Thinking mode took 254.2 s to fit against 0.069 s for logistic regression.
limits: One stratified split with a fixed seed and no interval; a lead of this size can be split noise.
TabPFN-2 and the full-data models saw different amounts of training data, so their tie is not a like-for-like comparison.
Telco churn lacks the prediction time, so even this clean comparison is a development estimate.
Thinking mode runs on a hosted service; its fit time depends on that service and was measured once.

measurements.name: TabPFN benchmark on HyperAck
measurements.gate: Same split for every model; compare ROC-AUC.
measurements.result: TabPFN thinking mode 0.981, histogram boosting 0.973, both with the leaky final fares in the inputs.
measurements.next: Discard these numbers as evidence; rerun with the fares removed.
measurements.against_gate: There is no threshold, and none could apply: TabPFN in thinking mode at 0.981 and histogram boosting at 0.973 both include the final fares, so the numbers measure the leak as much as the models.
limits: Leakage need not inflate every model by the same amount, so even the ranking cannot be trusted.

outcome: On Telco churn TabPFN in thinking mode gave the best ranking (0.850) with no tuning, about +0.009 over logistic regression. The HyperAck result is invalid until rerun without the final fares.
lessons: Every loader of a dataset must apply that dataset's contract; a leak fixed in one suite survives in a script written earlier.
risks: A loader written before a dataset's contract that still passes post-outcome columns.
The hosted model's API token committed in code or pasted in chat.
Comparing an untuned model with tuned baselines on one split and calling a small gap a win.
Judging the pretrained model on score alone, ignoring its latency and its data-size limits.
